topic: 决策偏差：人做判断时会被「前一个样本」带偏（Simonsohn 的面试评分研究）
text:
People are, on the whole, poor at considering background information when making individual decisions. At first glance this might seem like a strength that [[1]] the ability to make judgments which are unbiased by [[2]] factors. But Dr Simonsohn speculated that an inability to consider the big [[3]] was leading decision-makers to be biased by the daily samples of information they were working with. [[4]], he theorised that a judge [[5]] of appearing too soft [[6]] crime might be more likely to send someone to prison [[7]] he had already sentenced five or six other defendants only to forced community service on that day.

To [[8]] this idea, they turned their attention to the university-admissions process. In theory, the [[9]] of an applicant should not depend on the few others [[10]] randomly for interview during the same day, but Dr Simonsohn suspected the truth was [[11]].

He studied the results of 9,323 MBA interviews [[12]] by 31 admissions officers. The interviewers had [[13]] applicants on a scale of one to five. This scale [[14]] numerous factors into consideration. The scores were [[15]] used in conjunction with an applicant's score on the GMAT, a standardised exam which is [[16]] out of 800 points, to make a decision on whether to accept him or her.

Dr Simonsohn found if the score of the previous candidate in a daily series of interviewees was 0.75 points or more higher than that of the one [[17]] that, then the score for the next applicant would [[18]] by an average of 0.075 points. This might sound small, but to [[19]] the effects of such a decrease a candidate would need 30 more GMAT points than would otherwise have been [[20]].

blanks.answerNote: 原卷 D 项印作 dilivers（delivers 的错拼），照抄不改，方便你对着试卷找。
blanks.signal: that（定语从句）
blanks.explain: 空前的 strength（优势）与空后的 the ability 是「给予—被给予」关系：优势**赋予**能力。grant sb. sth. 正是「赋予某人某物」。

whyWrong.B: submit 提交（文件、申请），宾语不能是 ability。
whyWrong.C: transmit 传输（信号、疾病），宾语不能是 ability。
whyWrong.D: deliver 递送（货物）、发表（演讲），也不接 ability。

blanks.collocation: grant sb. sth. 赋予某人某物；grant that… 承认……

blanks.signal: background information（同义复现）
blanks.explain: 本空是首句 background information 的**同义复现**：判断不受「自身之外的信息」影响，即 external factors（外部因素）。完形答案优先选原词/同根复现，这是硬规律。

whyWrong.A: minor 次要的——与「背景信息」的语义词性都不对应，更不能解释「偏差」。
whyWrong.C: crucial 关键的——语义过重，「不受关键因素影响」在逻辑上说不通。
whyWrong.D: objective 客观的——被「客观因素」影响本身不构成 bias（偏差），逻辑反了。

blanks.collocation: external factors 外部因素；external influence 外来影响

blanks.signal: the big ___（固定短语）
blanks.explain: the big picture 是死搭配，意为「全局、整体」。整句在说：问题不是看不见「某个议题」，而是看不见**全局**——正好接住上一句的 background information。

whyWrong.A: issue 议题——the big issue 是「大问题」，但下文讲的是「视野窄」，不是「问题大」。
whyWrong.B: vision 视野/视力——the big vision 不是英语固定说法。

blanks.collocation: the big picture 全局；look at the big picture 看全局

blanks.signal: 上一句 theorised → 本句具体场景
blanks.explain: 上一句是抽象论断（看不见全局 ⇒ 决策有偏差），本句立刻摆出「法官量刑」的**具体场景**来落地，标准举例关系，只有 For example 能承上启下。

whyWrong.A: Above all 首先/最重要的是——递进，不举例。
whyWrong.B: On average 平均而言——统计口径，这里没在算平均。
whyWrong.C: In principle 原则上——表限定/让步，与「举例」无关。

blanks.collocation: for example / for instance 例如

blanks.signal: ___ of appearing too soft
blanks.explain: be fearful of doing sth. = 生怕/担心做某事。整句讲法官的**心理动机**：怕被舆论说「对罪犯太手软」，所以宁可重判。

whyWrong.A: be fond of 喜爱——褒义，与「怕显得手软」矛盾。
whyWrong.C: be capable of 能够——只表能力，不表担心，接不出后半句的因果。
whyWrong.D: thoughtless 欠考虑的——形容词，不能接 of appearing 表心理状态。

blanks.collocation: be fearful of (doing) sth. 生怕、担心

blanks.signal: soft ___ crime
blanks.explain: be soft on sb./sth. 是固定表达「对……心慈手软」，此处 soft on crime = 对犯罪手软。介词题只认搭配，不认语感。

whyWrong.C: soft to 不成立（to 常与 kind/polite 搭配）。

blanks.collocation: be soft on sb./sth. 对……手软 ⟷ be hard on 对……严厉

blanks.signal: might be more likely to … ___ he had already sentenced
blanks.explain: 空前后是「已经轻判了五六个 ⇒ 这一个更可能重判」的条件—结果关系，if 引导条件状语从句，与前面的 might be more likely 构成「如果……就更可能……」。

whyWrong.B: until 直到——时间终点，语义不通。
whyWrong.C: though 虽然——让步，会变成「虽然他轻判过」，逻辑断裂。
whyWrong.D: unless = if not——否定条件，意思正好反了。

blanks.collocation: if 条件从句 + 主句情态动词（might/could/would）

blanks.signal: To ___ this idea, they turned their attention to…
blanks.explain: 后文是「他们把注意力转向录取流程、去查 9,323 次面试」，动作是**检验**一个假设。test an idea / test a hypothesis 是最贴切的搭配。

whyWrong.B: emphasize 强调——强调不需要去查 9,323 个样本。
whyWrong.C: share 分享——他们本来就在同一个研究里，无分享对象。
whyWrong.D: promote 推广——一个还没验证的猜想谈不上推广。

blanks.collocation: test a hypothesis / an idea 检验假设

blanks.signal: the ___ of an applicant should not depend on
blanks.explain: 空处是「申请者」在录取语境下的**结果**：能不能被录取（success）。与后文 make a decision on whether to accept him or her 严格对应。

whyWrong.A: decision——决定是招生官做出的，不是申请者「拥有」并「取决于别人」的东西。
whyWrong.B: quality 素质——素质跟「同一天随机抽到谁」无关，句子会失去意义。
whyWrong.C: status 身份地位——申请者还没入学，谈不上身份。

blanks.collocation: the success of an applicant 申请者能否成功（被录取）

blanks.signal: the few others ___ randomly for interview
blanks.explain: others 与 choose 是**被动**关系：被随机抽来面试的另外几个人。过去分词 chosen 作后置定语，等于 who were chosen。

whyWrong.A: found 被发现——「被发现来面试」不通。
whyWrong.B: studied 被研究——此处说的是抽人，不是研究人。
whyWrong.D: identified 被识别——语义偏移，且 identify 通常要接 as。

blanks.collocation: those chosen for interview 被选中面试的人

blanks.signal: but … suspected the truth was ___
blanks.explain: but 表转折：「理论上不该如此，但 Simonsohn 怀疑事实**并非如此**」。otherwise 作表语 = not so，「不是这样的」，这是它在本篇唯一的用法。

whyWrong.B: defensible 可辩护的——「事实是可辩护的」讲不通。
whyWrong.C: replaceable 可替换的——与前文「不应取决于别人」不搭。
whyWrong.D: exceptional 例外的——形容词作表语虽合法，但不表达「与理论相反」这一层转折。

blanks.collocation: the truth was otherwise 事实并非如此；say otherwise 说不是这样

blanks.signal: interviews ___ by 31 admissions officers
blanks.explain: conduct an interview 是死搭配「主持/进行面试」。此处过去分词作后置定语：由 31 位招生官**主持**的 9,323 次面试。

whyWrong.A: inspired by 被……启发——搭配错。
whyWrong.B: expressed 表达——interview 不是被表达出来的。
whyWrong.D: secured 获得——语义与语法都不对。

blanks.collocation: conduct an interview / a survey / an experiment 进行面试/调查/实验

blanks.signal: on a scale of one to five
blanks.explain: on a scale of one to five（按 1–5 分制）直接锁定「打分、评级」义：rate sb. on a scale 是标准搭配。

whyWrong.A: assign 分配——assign sb. sth. 分配任务，后面不接 on a scale。
whyWrong.C: match 匹配——match A with B，没有「打分」义。
whyWrong.D: arrange 安排——arrange for sb. to do，与分数无关。

blanks.collocation: rate sb. on a scale of 1 to 5 按 1–5 分给某人打分

blanks.signal: ___ numerous factors into consideration
blanks.explain: take sth. into consideration 是固定短语「把……考虑在内」，此处宾语 numerous factors 提前，构成 take … into consideration 的完整式。

whyWrong.A: put 一般配 put sth. into practice（付诸实践），不接 into consideration。
whyWrong.D: give 要写成 give consideration to sth.，介词是 to 不是 into。

blanks.collocation: take sth. into consideration = take account of 把……考虑在内

blanks.signal: The scores were ___ used in conjunction with…
blanks.explain: 前面说「面试官先打分」，这句说「分数**随后**再与 GMAT 结合」，是步骤上的先后，then 表「然后」。

whyWrong.A: instead 相反/而是——表替代，这里没有「不这样而那样」。
whyWrong.C: ever 曾经——与 were used 的时态冲突。
whyWrong.D: rather 宁可——只有 rather than 结构才成立。

blanks.collocation: then 表先后：先……然后……

blanks.signal: which is ___ out of 800 points
blanks.explain: be marked out of 800 points = 按 800 分制计分。mark 在英式英语里就是「评分、计分」，out of 表「满分是」。

whyWrong.A: selected 被挑选——与分数制无关。
whyWrong.B: passed 被通过——考试通过不说 out of 800 points。
whyWrong.D: introduced 被引入——语法通、语义空。

blanks.collocation: be marked out of 100 按百分制计分

blanks.signal: that of the one ___ that
blanks.explain: the one before that = 「那之前的那个」，指**再前一位**考生。整句在比「前一位」与「再前一位」的分差，所以必须是 before。

whyWrong.A: below 在……之下——表位置高低。
whyWrong.B: after 在……之后——方向反了，会变成「后一位」。
whyWrong.C: above 在……之上——表位置高低。

blanks.collocation: the one before that 那之前的那个；the day before 前一天

blanks.signal: higher than … would ___ by an average of 0.075
blanks.explain: 前文说前一位**高出** 0.75 分，那么下一位的分数就**下降**——drop by 0.075 points「下降了 0.075 分」。前后构成一升一降的反向对照。

whyWrong.C: fluctuate 波动——只表来回变，不表单向下降。

blanks.collocation: drop by + 幅度 下降了……；rise by + 幅度 上升了……

blanks.signal: to ___ the effects of such a decrease
blanks.explain: undo 的僻义是「**抵消、使失效**」（不是「撤销」）。要抵消这 0.075 分下降带来的影响，考生得多考 30 分 GMAT——语义严丝合缝。

whyWrong.A: achieve 实现——不能「实现影响」来对抗下降。
whyWrong.D: disregard 忽视——忽视影响就不需要多考 30 分了。

blanks.collocation: undo the damage/effects 消除损害/影响

blanks.signal: than would otherwise have been ___（虚拟语气）
blanks.explain: than would otherwise have been necessary 是**虚拟语气**：「比原本所需的分数多 30 分」。necessary 与句中 need 语义呼应，是唯一能成立的选项。

whyWrong.C: promising 有前途的——修饰人/前景，不修饰分数。
whyWrong.D: helpful 有帮助的——「本来会有帮助的分数」逻辑不成立。

blanks.collocation: than necessary 比所需的（更多）；otherwise 与虚拟语气连用

sentences.en: People are, on the whole, poor at considering background information when making individual decisions.
sentences.zh: 总体而言，人们在做出个体决定时，并不擅长考虑背景信息。
sentences.struct: 主干：People are poor at considering…（be poor at doing 不擅长做某事）。on the whole 是插入语，把 are 和表语硬切开；when making = when they make，状语从句省略主语+be。

chunks.r: 时间状语（省略 they are）

sentences.en: At first glance this might seem like a strength that [[1]] the ability to make judgments which are unbiased by [[2]] factors.
sentences.zh: 乍一看，这似乎是一种优势——它赋予人一种能力，使人作出的判断不受外部因素影响。
sentences.struct: 主句：this might seem like a strength。that 引导定语从句修饰 strength，从句谓语就是第 1 空；to make judgments 是 ability 的后置定语；which 再引一个定语从句修饰 judgments。两个从句套在同一个名词短语上，是本篇最典型的「从句套从句」。

chunks.t: this might seem like a strength

chunks.r: 不定式作 ability 的后置定语

sentences.en: But Dr Simonsohn speculated that an inability to consider the big [[3]] was leading decision-makers to be biased by the daily samples of information they were working with.
sentences.zh: 但 Simonsohn 博士推测，正是这种无法顾及「全局」的缺陷，使决策者被他们日常处理的信息样本带偏。
sentences.struct: 主句 Dr Simonsohn speculated，后接 that 宾语从句。从句主语是 an inability（to consider… 作后置定语），谓语 was leading sb. to do（导致某人做某事）。by the daily samples 是被动来源；they were working with 是省略 that 的定语从句，修饰 information。

chunks.t: that an inability to consider the big [[3]]
chunks.r: 宾语从句主语 + 后置定语

chunks.t: was leading decision-makers to be biased
chunks.r: 从句谓语：lead sb. to do

chunks.t: by the daily samples of information

chunks.r: 省略 that 的定语从句（修饰 information）

sentences.en: [[4]], he theorised that a judge [[5]] of appearing too soft [[6]] crime might be more likely to send someone to prison [[7]] he had already sentenced five or six other defendants only to forced community service on that day.
sentences.zh: 举个例子，他提出这样的理论：一位生怕对犯罪显得过于手软的法官，如果当天已经把另外五六个被告仅仅判处强制社区服务，那么他就更可能把某个人送进监狱。
sentences.struct: 主句 he theorised + that 宾语从句。从句主语 a judge 带两个后置修饰：fearful of appearing too soft on crime（形容词短语）；谓语 might be more likely to send…to prison（be likely to do）。if 引导条件状语从句，only to forced community service 的 only 是「仅仅」，凸显前案轻判，才反衬出后案的从重。

chunks.t: that a judge [[5]] of appearing too soft [[6]] crime
chunks.r: 宾语从句主语 + 形容词短语后置定语

chunks.t: might be more likely to send someone to prison
chunks.r: 从句谓语：be likely to do

chunks.t: [[7]] he had already sentenced five or six other defendants

sentences.en: To [[8]] this idea, they turned their attention to the university-admissions process.
sentences.zh: 为了检验这一想法，他们把注意力转向了大学录取过程。
sentences.struct: To do 作目的状语前置；主句 they turned their attention to + 宾语（turn one's attention to 把注意力转向）。

sentences.en: In theory, the [[9]] of an applicant should not depend on the few others [[10]] randomly for interview during the same day, but Dr Simonsohn suspected the truth was [[11]].
sentences.zh: 理论上，一个申请者能否被录取，不应取决于当天随机抽来面试的另外几个人；但 Simonsohn 博士怀疑事实恰恰相反。
sentences.struct: but 连接两个并列分句。前分句主干 the [[9]] of an applicant should not depend on the few others；chosen randomly for interview 是过去分词短语作 others 的后置定语。后分句 suspected 后接省略 that 的宾语从句 the truth was [[11]]，otherwise 作表语。

chunks.t: the few others [[10]] randomly for interview
chunks.r: 宾语 + 过去分词后置定语
宾语从句（表语为第 11 空）

sentences.en: He studied the results of 9,323 MBA interviews [[12]] by 31 admissions officers.
sentences.zh: 他研究了由 31 位招生官主持的 9,323 次 MBA 面试的结果。
sentences.struct: 主干 He studied the results。of 9,323 MBA interviews 作 results 的后置定语；conducted by… 过去分词短语再修饰 interviews，形成「套娃式」后置定语。

chunks.r: 过去分词短语作后置定语

sentences.en: The interviewers had [[13]] applicants on a scale of one to five.
sentences.zh: 面试官按 1 到 5 分的量表给申请者打了分。
sentences.struct: 过去完成时 had + 过去分词（第 13 空）；on a scale of one to five 是方式状语，正是它锁定 rate 这个动词。

chunks.t: on a scale of one to five

sentences.en: This scale [[14]] numerous factors into consideration.
sentences.zh: 这一评分标准把诸多因素都纳入了考虑。
sentences.struct: 主谓宾结构：This scale [[14]] numerous factors into consideration。take sth. into consideration 被拆开，宾语插在中间，这是固定短语的常见考法。

sentences.en: The scores were [[15]] used in conjunction with an applicant's score on the GMAT, a standardised exam which is [[16]] out of 800 points, to make a decision on whether to accept him or her.
sentences.zh: 随后，这些分数会与申请者的 GMAT 成绩（一项按 800 分制计分的标准化考试）结合使用，以决定是否录取他/她。
sentences.struct: 主干 The scores were used（被动）+ then 表先后。in conjunction with… 是方式状语（与……结合）；a standardised exam 是 GMAT 的同位语，which 引导定语从句修饰它；to make a decision 是目的状语，on whether to accept… 作 decision 的后置定语（whether + 不定式）。

chunks.t: in conjunction with an applicant's score on the GMAT
a standardised exam which is [[16]] out of 800 points
to make a decision on whether to accept him or her

sentences.en: Dr Simonsohn found if the score of the previous candidate in a daily series of interviewees was 0.75 points or more higher than that of the one [[17]] that, then the score for the next applicant would [[18]] by an average of 0.075 points.
sentences.zh: Simonsohn 博士发现：如果当天连续面试的考生中，前一位的分数比再前一位高出 0.75 分或更多，那么下一位申请者的分数平均就会下降 0.075 分。
sentences.struct: found 后接「if…then…」条件主从复合句（省略了宾语从句引导词 that）。比较结构 was 0.75 points or more higher than that of the one before that 里，that 代替 the score，避免重复。主句 would drop by an average of 0.075 points：by 表幅度。

chunks.t: if the score of the previous candidate … was 0.75 points or more higher than that of the one [[17]] that
chunks.r: 条件状语从句（含比较结构）

chunks.t: then the score for the next applicant would [[18]]

sentences.en: This might sound small, but to [[19]] the effects of such a decrease a candidate would need 30 more GMAT points than would otherwise have been [[20]].
sentences.zh: 这个数字听起来很小，但要抵消这种分数下降带来的影响，考生需要比原本所需的分数多考 30 分 GMAT。
sentences.struct: but 连接两个分句。前分句 This might sound small 是系表结构。后分句 to undo… 为目的状语前置，主干 a candidate would need 30 more GMAT points；than would otherwise have been necessary 是**比较状语从句 + 虚拟语气**，省略了主语 the points，otherwise 与虚拟式连用表「原本会」。

chunks.r: 前分句：主 + 系 + 表

chunks.t: but to [[19]] the effects of such a decrease
a candidate would need 30 more GMAT points

chunks.r: 比较状语从句（省略 the points，虚拟语气）

fullZh: 总体而言，人们在做出个体决定时并不擅长考虑背景信息。乍一看，这似乎是一种优势——它赋予人一种能力，使人作出的判断不受外部因素影响。但 Simonsohn 博士推测，正是这种无法顾及「全局」的缺陷，使决策者被他们日常处理的信息样本带偏。举个例子，他提出这样的理论：一位生怕对犯罪显得过于手软的法官，如果当天已经把另外五六个被告仅仅判处强制社区服务，那么他就更可能把某个人送进监狱。
为了检验这一想法，他们把注意力转向了大学录取过程。理论上，一个申请者能否被录取，不应取决于当天随机抽来面试的另外几个人；但 Simonsohn 博士怀疑事实恰恰相反。
他研究了由 31 位招生官主持的 9,323 次 MBA 面试的结果。面试官按 1 到 5 分的量表给申请者打了分，这一评分标准把诸多因素都纳入了考虑。随后，这些分数会与申请者的 GMAT 成绩（一项按 800 分制计分的标准化考试）结合使用，以决定是否录取他/她。
Simonsohn 博士发现：如果当天连续面试的考生中，前一位的分数比再前一位高出 0.75 分或更多，那么下一位申请者的分数平均就会下降 0.075 分。这个数字听起来很小，但要抵消这种分数下降带来的影响，考生需要比原本所需的分数多考 30 分 GMAT。

takeaways: 本篇 20 空里，**逻辑关系题 5 道**（4、7、15、17、18），全部靠「空前后同向还是反向」就能定，一个生词都不需要认识。
**固定搭配 6 道**（3、5、6、12、14，加第 1 空的双宾语）——the big picture / be fearful of / be soft on / conduct an interview / take sth. into consideration。这一块是性价比最高的 3 分。
第 2 空 external 是「原词复现」：与首句 background information 同指「外部信息」。完形答案优先选原词/同根复现，**不是**同义替换——这是完形和阅读最大的区别。
第 19 空 undo 是「熟词僻义」：undo = 抵消，不是「撤销」。背单词必须记第二义项，考研完形每年至少 2 个这种坑。
全文只有一个论点：人做判断会被「前一个样本」带偏（序列效应 / 锚定）。读懂这一句，13–20 空基本是白给；读不懂，就会在 drop / jump 这种方向题上反复。
做题顺序建议：先扫第 2 空（复现）、第 3 空（the big picture）、第 12 空（conduct an interview）这三个白给的，把文章骨架立住，再回头啃第 9、11、19 空。
